Self-rated knowledge questions draw few "don't know" answers, since respondents can always judge their own knowledge. Employees answering a web survey also tend to be engaged, which pushes the share lower still. Comparable Eurobarometer-style items usually show 1–3% "don't know"; the visible on-screen option nudges this toward the upper middle of that range.

[1.8]

This item asks about the respondent's own economic situation, which most people can evaluate, so don't-know rates tend to be very low. Even with an explicit DK option displayed, only a small share of respondents would choose it, probably around 1%.

[1.0]

This is a Eurobarometer-style item, but in a self-administered web survey with DK explicitly displayed. Eurobarometer face-to-face DK for national economy is typically ~1-2%. For web surveys with a visible DK option, the rate is probably a bit higher, around 2-4%.

[2.5]

This looks like a Eurobarometer-style item. In Standard Eurobarometer face-to-face surveys, "DK" on the expectation for the EU economy runs about 8-12%. In a web survey with DK explicitly displayed, the share is probably similar or somewhat higher, since respondents can easily pick it. EU economy expectations are harder to judge than national or personal ones, so DK would be higher for this item. I estimate about 9%.

[9.0]

This looks like a Eurobarometer-style item, though the web mode with an explicit DK option may raise DK rates relative to face-to-face. In Standard Eurobarometer, DK on the EU economy runs about 5-8%. For a self-administered web survey with DK explicitly displayed, I'd estimate it slightly higher, around 7%.

[7.0]

This question asks employees about cyber exposure of their own sector, which many may not know well. With an explicit DK option in a web survey, DK rates for such perception items typically run 10-20%. For the sector in which the organisation operates, I'd estimate around 14%.

[14.0]

This is a Eurobarometer-style youth survey item. The question asks for a comparison with 30 years ago, which many young people (15-30) may find hard to judge since they weren't alive. Don't know is likely elevated, perhaps around 8-10%.

[8.5]

This looks like a Flash Eurobarometer youth survey item. Young people often select "Don't know" on political evaluation statements, typically 8-15%. For a statement about policymakers considering long-term consequences, which is fairly abstract, I'd estimate around 10%.

[10.5]

This is a Flash Eurobarometer on youth. A future-oriented statement like this one tends to draw a moderately high "Don't know" share, probably in the 6-10% range. I'll estimate 7.

[7.5]

This is a Eurobarometer-style prospective economic expectations question. In face-to-face Eurobarometer, DK for national economy in 12 months is roughly 5-8%. In a web survey with DK explicitly displayed, it would be a bit higher possibly, though web respondents tend to be more engaged. I estimate about 7%.

[7.0]

This resembles a Eurobarometer-style item, but in a self-administered web mode with an explicit DK option. For the national economy rating, DK rates are typically low in Eurobarometer face-to-face, around 1-2%. In web surveys with an explicit DK shown, rates tend to be a bit higher, perhaps 2-4%.

[2.5]

This resembles Eurobarometer questions, where "don't know" for the EU economy is typically around 5-8% in face-to-face surveys. In a web survey with DK explicitly displayed, the rate is likely similar or slightly higher, since evaluating the EU economy is harder than the national economy.

[6.5]

This resembles the Eurobarometer item on expectations for the EU economy; in face-to-face surveys, DK rates for such items are around 8-12%. In a web mode with an explicit DK option shown, the rate would likely be similar or somewhat higher, since there is no interviewer pushing for an answer. Forecasting the EU economy is difficult, so DK is plausible at around 10%.

[9.5]

This resembles Eurobarometer-style questions on expectations for personal economic situation. In the Standard Eurobarometer, DK for "financial situation of your household" in 12 months is typically about 3-6%. For a web survey with an explicit DK option, the rate might be slightly higher, around 5-8%. "Your economic situation" in this wording is likely from the European Parliament Eurobarometer or the Eurobarometer on life in the EU. I'd estimate about 5%.

[5.0]

Reasoning: EU surveys like Eurobarometer typically have DK around 5-10% for economic effect questions. In web surveys with explicit DK option, probably around 7%.

[7.5]

This is a behavioral question about the respondent's own habits, which people can almost always answer. Don't know rates for such items in web surveys with an explicit DK option are typically low, and some employees may not have a computer or workstation, which could inflate the DK selection slightly.

[2.5]

This looks like a Eurobarometer-style question about cyber threat exposure, asked here in a web survey of employees. The item asks about the respondent's own sector, which most employees can judge reasonably well. Some will not know, particularly in sectors where cyber risk is less visible.

Don't know rates for this kind of item typically run around 8-15%. Because the "Don't know" option is explicitly displayed, and the question is about sectoral exposure that is somewhat abstract, I estimate about 10%.

[10.5]

This is from the Eurobarometer youth survey (Flash Eurobarometer on youth, 2021-ish). The statement involves comparison with 30 years ago, which for young people aged 15-30 is before they were born, so the "don't know" rate would likely be elevated, perhaps 8-12%.

I'll estimate around 9%.

[9.0]

This question asks about the respondent's own economic situation, which most people can easily assess, so "Don't know" should be rare. In Eurobarometer-type surveys, DK for personal situation is typically around 1%, and a web mode with an explicit DK option might raise it slightly.

[1.2]

This resembles Eurobarometer-style questions about expectations for the next 12 months. In face-to-face Eurobarometer, DK rates for national economy expectations are around 5-8%. In a web survey with an explicit DK option, the rate may be a bit higher or similar. Economic forecasting items tend to have moderate DK rates.

[7.0]

In Eurobarometer-type surveys, DK for EU economy evaluations is around 5-8% in face-to-face. In web surveys with explicit DK option, probably similar, maybe slightly higher for EU-level judgments.

[6.5]

This is from the Flash Eurobarometer on youth (2021 or 2024). Statement about future chances is a speculative question, so "don't know" is likely moderate, perhaps 8-12%.

In the Flash Eurobarometer 502 on Youth and democracy, DK rates for such statements were around 5-10%. For a forward-looking statement, I'd guess about 9%.

[8.5]

This looks like a Eurobarometer-style question about the national economy, which people usually have an opinion on. In Eurobarometer face-to-face surveys, DK for "situation of the national economy" is around 1-3%. In a web survey with the DK option displayed explicitly, it would be slightly higher, perhaps 2-3%.

[2.1]

This resembles the Eurobarometer-style question on expectations over the next 12 months. In Eurobarometer face-to-face, DK rates for EU economy outlook are around 8-12%. In a web survey with an explicit DK option, rates are probably similar or somewhat higher for the EU-level economy, since it's harder to judge than the national economy.

[9.5]

This resembles Eurobarometer-type questions, where DK rates for EU economic effect questions are typically around 5-10%. In a web survey with an explicit DK option and no neutral midpoint, the DK share may be somewhat higher. I estimate about 8%.

[8.0]

This is an estimate of the "don't know" share for a question about how exposed the respondent's own sector is to cyber threats, in a web survey of EU employees where a "Don't know / no answer" option is shown explicitly.

Judgment from comparable items: respondents tend to have an opinion about their own organisation's sector, but some are unsure. In Eurobarometer-style surveys, "don't know" rates for sector-level assessments typically run around 8-15%. Web mode with an explicit DK option tends to raise that figure.

[11.5]

This appears to be a Eurobarometer-style youth survey item. Comparing chances with those 30 years ago is a hard question for people aged 15-30, who did not live then, so Don't know could be notably elevated. Typical DK rates for such items are around 8-12%.

[10.5]

This is from a Eurobarometer-style youth survey (Flash Eurobarometer on youth, web-based). Don't know on a future-oriented opinion statement is typically moderate. For similar items, DK rates tend to be around 5-10%. The statement about chances in 30 years' time is somewhat abstract, so I'd estimate about 7%.

[7.0]
